articles.title: Maine tenants challenged rent increases under Portland’s rent-control law; after a union campaign and 20 hours of mediation, their landlord agreed to a $3.6 million settlement to reimburse more than 1,000 renters
articles.summary: The tenants’ union in Portland, Maine, has reached a $3.6 million settlement with local landlord Geoffrey Rice, who was accused of illegally raising
articles.body: The tenants’ union in Portland, Maine, has reached a $3.6 million settlement with local landlord Geoffrey Rice, who was accused of illegally raising rents, according to a report by Realtor.com. Trelawny Tenants Union (TTU) and Rice reached the multimillion-dollar settlement on Sunday after years of disputes and 20 hours of mediation. Under the terms, more than 1,000 current and former tenants will be reimbursed for excess rent paid since 2020. The settlement covers nearly $3 million in overcharged rent, as well as additional fines.A union born in the pandemicThe Trelawny Tenants Union started during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020 as a ‘mutual aid’ group among neighbours, according to TTU treasurer Ethan Strimling, a tenant in one of Rice’s buildings and a former Portland mayor. “We never could have done this if it had been one person at a time trying to get Geoffrey to adjust their rent. Because tenants became represented by the union and so many people came to our meetings and participated in audits and actions and lobbied the city council, it has really shown what tenants can do when they come together,” Strimling told Maine Public.TTU’s members wanted to keep rent increases and evictions in check while COVID-19 squeezed household budgets. Initially, they tried to work with landlord Geoffrey Rice, who owns 19 properties in Portland with more than 300 units. However, that cooperation did not last. Rice repeatedly broke the city’s rent-control ordinance, which took effect on 1 January 2021, multiple reports suggest. The law limits annual rent increases. The cap is 70% of a regional inflation measure, with a hard ceiling of 10%.Twenty hours of mediationThe union and Rice had spent years going back and forth in court and before the city’s Rent Board. Last week, they sat down for 20 hours of mediation and finally reached a deal on Sunday.Under the terms, the landlord must roll rents back to the amounts allowed under the law’s December 2022 compliance standard across all 19 of his buildings. He will also deposit $3.6 million into an escrow account. About $2.86 million of that will reimburse more than 1,000 current and former residents who have paid more than the law allowed since June 2020.“It’s just a really big day for tenants. Really important day for affordability. Hopefully, other landlords will take notice and ensure they are in compliance with the law,” Strimling told the broadcaster.So where does the money go? The union will receive $230,000 to cover past and future costs. The city of Portland will collect a $250,000 fine. Another $260,000 will remain in reserve in case further overcharges come to light. When calculating refunds, the union found one unit where the rent was $300 a year above the legal limit in 2020. Refunds for that apartment alone will top $24,000, and the amount will be split among several tenants who lived there over the years. Strimling said the outcome was satisfactory, but implementing it might take time. He believes the $3.6 million will fairly compensate tenants for the amounts they were overcharged.The Portland Tenants Union (PTU) helped mediate the settlement. “We have had multiple cases where tenants are getting refunds in the thousands or even tens of thousands of dollars in rents they have paid that are not allowed,” PTU co-founder Bradley Davis told the broadcaster.The city council is calling for the rental registration system to be digitised, which would make it easier to flag violations, Davis added.You use AI every day. articles.title: US Midterm Polls: Democrats sniff opportunity, Trump fights to avoid a lame-duck presidency
articles.summary: As Americans head into the final stretch of campaigning for the Nov 3 US midterm polls, both Democratic and Republican parties are set to field their big
articles.body: As Americans head into the final stretch of campaigning for the Nov 3 US midterm polls, both Democratic and Republican parties are set to field their big guns – and go on an ad-blitz – across key battleground states. Weighing on voters’ minds are issues like the rising cost of living, Trump’s war against Iran that has seen fuel prices skyrocket, healthcare and housing. Here’s a quick primer on what’s at stake in the polls, why it could be hugely consequential for the Trump presidency, and how it may shape US foreign policy.Betting on the House: All 435 seats in Congress’s House of Representatives are up for grabs. Republicans hold a slim majority of 218 to Democrats’ 214 in the House. But this is widely expected to flip. That hinges on about 50 competitive races. Pollsters say Democrats could end up with a majority of as many as 15 seats.Senatorial action: But it’s the Senate races that will determine whether Trump’s agenda over the next two years sinks or floats. The chamber has only 100 seats, but senators have staggered six-year terms. That means only 35 seats are up for grabs this time, of which about 10 are really competitive and likely to flip. If Democrats snag them up, they will overturn Republicans’ current majority of 53 to 45. Which is precisely why Republicans are pulling out all stops to boost their candidates in key races.If Dems get House, GOP holds Senate: A likely scenario, although Republicans have been shaken up by reported close contests in red states like Texas and Kansas. Plus, Trump’s approval rating is down – a record low for him at 31% in the latest poll. So, Republicans are divided over associating themselves with Trump’s policies. For some, getting the President’s endorsement may actually spell doom in tight races.But if Republicans do manage to hold onto their majority in Senate, Trump would still have room to manoeuvre and, more importantly, bat down political challenges emanating from a Democrats-dominated House.If Dems win both houses: That’s the nightmare scenario Trump and GOP are trying to avoid. If Democrats control both the House and Senate, they effectively gain control of the legislative agenda. Sure, Democrats would still have to contend with Trump’s veto power – he could use that to block any Democrats-led legislation. And overturning a presidential veto requires two-thirds majority in both houses – a rarity.But Democrats could still prove a point by forcing Trump to exercise his veto. That in turn could have political implications for presidential polls in 2028, putting Republicans looking for a post-Trump future in a tight spot. Also, unlike the House where a simple majority passes legislation, for bills to pass Senate they require a supermajority of 60 votes. Still, this is a scenario that GOP would like to avoid at all costs.Key races: Naturally, most of them focus on Senate seats.In North Carolina, Democratic candidate Roy Cooper is leading in the polls over Republican candidate Michael Whatley. This is a seat GOP appears to be giving up on, holding back on ad spends in the final two weeks. Texas is turning out to be a humdinger. Polls show a tight race between Democrat James Talarico and Republican Ken Paxton. Talarico is pegged to be slightly ahead at this point. And if he pulls it off on election day, Dems would end their 32-year losing streak in the state. But Republicans are pouring big money into this race, and are slated to outspend Democrats by three times, with overall GOP ad spend on this race set to cross $380mn. Kansas, likewise, is witnessing a neck-to-neck race where Democrat Adam Hamilton is squaring off against GOP senator Roger Marshall. Recent polls showed there’s practically nothing to separate the two candidates. If Democrats win here, it would be historic – the state hasn’t elected a Democratic senator in 94 years. The race in Michigan is grabbing a lot of eyeballs, thanks to Democratic candidate Abdul El-Sayed who is going up against Republican Mike Rogers. Trump himself has taken potshots at El-Sayed, calling him a Muslim radical, while other Republican leaders have tried to associate him with the Muslim Brotherhood. If El-Sayed wins, he would be the first Muslim senator in US history. Impact on US foreign policy: If Democrats win back both houses, it would certainly reduce space for Trump to act unilaterally on the foreign policy front. However, there are many ways in which Trump could work around any restrictions. For example, his war against Iran has skirted around the 60-day window for congressional approval through White House’s clever classification of the military action as aimed at ‘protecting American people’. Trump has also argued that since the war has started and stopped several times, the 60-day window for approval has renewed each time.However, if Democrats control Congress, they could curtail any funding for that war. Conversely, they could also try to fast track funding support for Ukraine. But Trump could veto that or simply not act. So, it could be a stalemate between Trump and a Democrats-controlled Congress.A third impeachment: A nuclear option, but not beyond the realm of possibility if Democrats win Congress. More likely though would be Democrats taking control of several committees, launching investigations against Trump officials or Trump family members, and blocking Trump’s appointments to key govt positions and roles, essentially leading to a lame-duck presidency.You use AI every day. articles.title: UP polls: Congress shares initial list with SP, seeks 175-200 seats
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Congress has formally begun seat-sharing negotiations with the Samajwadi Party (SP) in poll-bound Uttar Pradesh, submitting an initial list
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Congress has formally begun seat-sharing negotiations with the Samajwadi Party (SP) in poll-bound Uttar Pradesh, submitting an initial list of more than 175 assembly constituencies to the Akhilesh Yadav-led party.Rajendra Pal Gautam, the Congress’ in-charge for Uttar Pradesh, told PTI that the list was shared with SP leaders around two days ago. He added that leaders from both parties would soon hold detailed discussions on the nature of a seat-sharing arrangement.“I can't give you the exact numbers, but we have submitted a list for 175 to 200 seats. The leadership of both parties will sit together to thrash out the nitty-gritties of the seat-sharing arrangement," Gautam said.The Congress has reportedly classified constituencies based on an assessment of its electoral prospects, and seat-sharing negotiations are expected to centre on this assessment.Scepticism within SP over Congress’ seat demandsHowever, several SP leaders remain unconvinced that the Congress has enough political clout to demand 175-200 seats, despite their successful alliance in Uttar Pradesh during the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.The scepticism stems from the Congress’ declining electoral fortunes in Uttar Pradesh since 1989, when it last held power in the country’s most populous state.“I think our party leader Akhilesh Yadav has made it clear that winnability is the sole criterion (for contesting the polls). Anyone can demand anything, but in politics, to reach an acceptable and meaningful solution, you have to move beyond posturing,” a senior SP leader told PTI.The Congress contested the 2022 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections independently but managed to win just two constituencies, down from seven in 2017, when it fought in alliance with the SP. That year, the SP lost power after a single term, securing only 47 seats, while the BJP won a landslide 312 seats in the 403-member ssembly.In 2022, the BJP retained power with 255 seats, while the SP won 111 constituencies.However, the 2024 Lok Sabha elections offered the Congress renewed hope. The grand old party won six seats in Uttar Pradesh, while the SP secured 37 of the state’s 80 seats, limiting the BJP to 33, down from 62 in 2019 and 71 in 2014. The results have strengthened the Congress’ expectations of securing a “respectable share” of seats in the 2027 assembly elections, party leaders acknowledged.“It’s obvious… The 2024 Lok Sabha results were proof that together the two parties can make an impact. In politics, there has to be room for meaningful give and take,” a senior Congress leader said.How the change in UP Congress leadership could influence seat-sharing talksThe recent leadership change in the Uttar Pradesh Congress, with Aradhana Misra “Mona” succeeding Ajay Rai as state unit chief, is also believed to have been factored into the party’s efforts to reach an amicable seat-sharing arrangement with the SP.Some believe Rai was not in favour of a pre-poll alliance, viewing a post-poll arrangement as a more suitable option for the Congress.However, some party leaders feel that Misra’s “excellent relations” with the SP leadership may have influenced the party’s decision to appoint her months ahead of the assembly elections, potentially facilitating negotiations between themThe Uttar Pradesh assembly elections are scheduled to be held in February-March next year.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Watch: Terrifying moment 18-storey building collapses in Kenya, many feared trapped
articles.summary: A multi-storey building under construction collapsed in Kenya’s capital, Nairobi, on Friday, leaving a massive pile of concrete and raising fears that
articles.body: A multi-storey building under construction collapsed in Kenya’s capital, Nairobi, on Friday, leaving a massive pile of concrete and raising fears that several people were trapped beneath the rubble.The building, which had more than 10 upper floors under construction, collapsed at around 1pm along a busy commercial street in the Eastleigh area. Footage from the scene showed the structure crumbling into a heap of debris, with multiple floors appearing to have collapsed on top of one another.The 18-storey building was located along 1st Avenue, 9th Street, in a densely populated neighbourhood frequented by traders and residents.Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja confirmed that one person had been rescued from the debris and taken to hospital. Emergency teams continued searching the site for others who may have been trapped.Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja, who visited the scene with county officials, said rescue workers were carefully clearing sections of the rubble to allow oxygen to reach people who might still be alive beneath the debris.According to an update from Nairobi City County, the building was still under construction when it collapsed, although its ground floor was already occupied.Sakaja said the structure did not comply with construction guidelines and vowed that legal action would be taken against its owner. Authorities are expected to investigate whether the building had the required approvals and met structural safety standards.The collapse triggered a major emergency response, with county teams deploying machinery to remove debris and create access routes for rescuers. The Kenya Red Cross also said its teams were on their way to the site and urged the public to give emergency responders enough space to work safely.Rescue operations were complicated by the large crowds gathering around the collapsed structure. Police fired tear gas to disperse onlookers and people who had begun looting neighbouring shops, as officers attempted to clear the area and prevent obstruction of emergency vehicles.Movement along 1st Avenue and 9th Street was disrupted as residents and traders rushed to the scene.You use AI every day. articles.summary: PATNA: Five persons were killed, while three others were injured after massive explosion took place in a house due to fire catching in firecrackers in
articles.body: PATNA: Five persons were killed, while three others were injured after massive explosion took place in a house due to fire catching in firecrackers in Siwan district on Friday.The incident occurred in Alampur village under Jamo Bazar police station area.Five bodies were recovered from the scene in the explosion that occurred around 5.30pm in the evening.Eight persons were reported to be in the house during the explosion. However, they escaped from the spot with minor burn injuries and rushed to local hospital. The explosion was so intense that debris of front part of house fell on road.Maharajganj SDPO, Aman Kumar informed that Md Amiruddin, 65, his two grand-daughters of 14 and eight years of age, a 10-year-old neighbour boy and an unidentified person were found dead.Taking strict note of the gravity of the incident and alleged local negligence, Siwan SP Bharat Soni ordered the immediate suspension of the Jamo Bazar SHO, Dhiraj kumar and local chowkidar Chandrika Manjhi.As per information, firecrackers were stored in the house of Alampur resident Mohd Amiruddin Mian, who is said to be a firecracker trader.The fire soon spread to other firecrackers stored there, triggering continuous explosions. Blast sounds were heard intermittently for about two hours.Panic gripped the nearby areas after the incident. People were terrified by the sound of explosions and chaos prevailed at the spot.Due to the damage to the house and the severity of the blast, relief and identification work faced difficulties.Senior officials, including the district magistrate (DM) of Siwan, Vijay Prakash Meena and the superintendent of police (SP), Bharat Soni visited the scene.A medical team, fire department, electricity department, dog squad, and a Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) team were deployed to cordon off the area and collect scientific evidence.Siwan DM Vijay Prakash Meena said information was being received about firecracker manufacturing in house. Explosion took place in the same house.SP Bharat Soni said five deaths had been confirmed so far, while the whereabouts of three other people remained uncertain as they left for some private hospitals on their own.They had reportedly received minor injuries. The figure of eight was based on information provided by local residents, including village representatives, and the authorities were awaiting further confirmation from the medical team, he said.“A special police team under the leadership of the SDPO Maharajganj, Aman Kumar has been formed to thoroughly investigate all aspects of the case. articles.summary: A 71-year-old man was killed after a Tesla operating in Full Self-Driving mode struck him while he was crossing a California freeway on October 22),
articles.body: A 71-year-old man was killed after a Tesla operating in Full Self-Driving mode struck him while he was crossing a California freeway on October 22), authorities said.The crash occurred around 2:30 am on westbound Interstate 80 in Vallejo, near the Interstate 780 interchange. The Tesla was travelling at around 70 mph (112 kmph) when the pedestrian entered the freeway from the right shoulder, according to a report by the San Francisco Chronicle.The driver, a 26-year-old man from San Francisco, told California Highway Patrol (CHP) officers that the vehicle's Full Self-Driving system was engaged at the time of the collision.Dashcam footage reviewed by investigators showed the Tesla applying its brakes and steering to the left in an attempt to avoid the pedestrian. However, the car's front-right portion struck the man, CHP said.The driver stopped at the scene and provided the recording to officers. The pedestrian was left lying in a traffic lane and was subsequently struck by at least one other vehicle. First responders determined that he had suffered fatal injuries. No other drivers stopped at the scene.CHP Officer Scott Heitman told the San Francisco Chronicle that the driver had not been cited. Authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding the crash, including why the pedestrian was on the freeway. Charges could still be considered if investigators establish that driver negligence contributed to the collision.Tesla describes Full Self-Driving (Supervised) as a driver-assistance system that can steer, change lanes and navigate intersections, but requires a fully attentive human driver who remains ready to take control. The system does not make a vehicle fully autonomous.Another Tesla crash on California freewayThe fatal crash comes days after a separate incident involving a Tesla using Full Self-Driving on Interstate 80 near Fairfield, California.On October 13, a Tesla struck a California Highway Patrol patrol vehicle, injuring two officers inside. The 22-year-old driver from Sacramento reportedly told officers that he had fallen asleep while using the system.Three CHP patrol vehicles had their emergency lights activated as officers responded to an earlier fatal collision, with four lanes closed at the time. The Tesla drove through safety cones before hitting a CHP Dodge Charger.The latest incident has renewed attention on the limitations of driver-assistance technology and the responsibility motorists retain when using such systems.CHP has urged anyone who witnessed the October 22 crash, or who has information about the other vehicles that struck the pedestrian, to contact its Solano Area office.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Ugh. They are Black': NYC broker typed text for property owners, mistakenly sent to the couple hunting for apartments
articles.summary: A couple has filed a lawsuit against a real estate brokerage company, an agent and several property owners after they said they were racially
articles.body: A couple has filed a lawsuit against a real estate brokerage company, an agent and several property owners after they said they were racially discriminated against when they were seeking to rent an apartment in Queens. A message that was meant to be sent only to the owners, cautioning them that the couple was Black was also sent to them by mistake, they claimed.According to Eyewitness News ABC7NY, Lisa Renee Olaso and her fiancée, Cyril Christopher, said they were excited to move to 26th Avenue in Flushing in June after relocating from Delaware because Olaso had a new job. They said a broker from Douglas Elliman was scheduled to meet them to show them a rental apartment. The broker did not meet them in person and only saw from a distance. Olaso said she was accidentally included on a text message intended for the property owner."As we were getting out of the car, I received the text message that said, 'Ugh. They are Black,'" Olaso said.The broker tried to control the damage and said there were previous episodes with Black tenants. "When she looked at her phone, she started to explain that there were previous, Black tenants in the neighborhood and that they had caused a lot of trouble," Olaso said.Olaso said the broker apologized, but the incident continues to affect her. The couple is suing Douglas Elliman Realty, Tzelios and several people listed as owners of the property. Their attorney Kenneth Mollins said the text message did not occur in isolation and so they included everyonein their lawsuit. "Unless the person receiving the text gets it in some context to know, why she's sending that. So, we believe the homeowner was in some way responsible here," Mollins said.In a statement provided Wednesday, a Douglas Elliman spokesperson said: "Douglas Elliman has a zero-tolerance policy for discrimination of any kind, and the agent is no longer with the company.""It's like judging a book by its cover. You haven't even read the book, and you already made a judgement call," Christopher said.Olaso said an apology from the broker did not ease the pain caused by the racial profiling."It doesn’t change the pain. articles.title: Storm Austen: Strong winds and heavy rain batter southern UK
articles.summary: On Saturday, Storm Boelo is forecast to bring more strong winds and heavy rain to Scotland and parts of northern England.
articles.body:
More than 19,000 homes are without power as Storm Austen continues to batter southern England and Wales.

The first named storm of the season brought gusts of up to 84mph (135km/h) to Jersey, while in southern England the wild weather disrupted travel with fallen trees blocking railway lines and roads.

In Brighton, part of the iconic West Pier - an abandoned structure that first opened in 1866 - collapsed into the sea.

On Saturday, Storm Boelo is forecast to bring more strong winds and heavy rain. The Met Office has put in place an amber warning for wind on Saturday and Sunday to cover parts of Scotland, northern England and Northern Ireland.

Austen made landfall in the south-west overnight and tracked eastwards throughout the day. All schools on Jersey and Guernsey closed for the day and some in Cornwall were closed or started later than normal.

Ahead of the worst of the storm on Thursday afternoon, families were evacuated from a holiday park in Perranporth, Cornwall. Among them was Hannah Dawson-Turk, who told the BBC "the night before last, it sounded like our caravan was going to be ripped apart".

"The storm is very loud outside now, and the waves look huge from our windows," she said from a nearby hotel.

In the south-west, around 13,000 properties were without power.

Some ferry services between the UK and France were cancelled, while National Rail advised many routes were travelling at slower speeds.

In Brighton, onlookers filmed as a section of the West Pier fell into the sea as it was pummeled by large waves.

Stephen Royle, who lives opposite, said the waves rolling in were "enormous" and he is "shocked" by how much of the pier ended up in the sea.

The pier closed to the public in 1975 and fell into disrepair, but the ruined structure became a symbol of Brighton for some.

On the Channel Islands, fresh food shortages are expected in the coming days due to a lack of ferry services, according to the boss of the Co-op there.

"It's rare we get this level of disruption to storms backing up so quickly and probably a little bit more heavier than what we've had to deal with in the past," Mark Cox said.

Paul Aked, head of Jersey Met, said there were gusts in Guernsey up to 76mph (122km/h), equivalent to a severe gale, force nine. Residents told BBC Radio Guernsey that they could hear the wind rattling through their homes.

Jersey Airport said flights won't be running "until at least 17:00" while Cornwall Airport Newquay is warning passengers to check with their airline before travel.

Departure boards at Exeter airport were showing multiple cancellations.

The UK will continue to be battered by strong winds and heavy rain over the weekend as Storm Boelo follows on the heels of Storm Austen.

The Met Office has issued an amber weather warning for wind for much of Scotland, excluding the Northern Isles, as well as the far north of Northern Ireland and England.

Wind gusts of 60-70mph are forecast, with exposed coastal areas potentially seeing speeds of up to 80mph.

The Central Lowlands could also experience disruption as strong winds funnel through the region.

Damage caused by strong winds could lead to further power cuts, while travel disruption is also predicted.

Yellow wind warnings also cover Orkney, the rest of Northern Ireland and northern England.

Gusts of 55-75mph are possible in these areas, with isolated gusts potentially reaching 80mph.

Alongside the strong winds, heavy and persistent rain is forecast across the UK on Saturday.

Spray and surface water could make driving conditions hazardous, while further downpours increase the risk of localised flooding.

The Met Office has advised the public to drive cautiously in strong wind, and to secure loose items outside their homes such as bins and trampolines.

People living or working in coastal areas were advised to take extra care during windy or stormy weather, including staying indoors as much as possible.

The storm came as the government released general advice for households to stock up on tinned food and bottled water in order to be prepared for emergencies.

The government has drawn up recommendations for households to have three days' worth of bottled water and tinned food to deal with a crisis such as a war, an online attack or a natural disaster.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said: "It's not about panic buying... It's about just taking sensible measures to have enough in the house to tide you over should there be a difficult situation."

Last month, the National Audit Office warned Britain's food supply chain is at risk given the growing threat of cyber-attacks and the climate crisis.

It said the Department for Food, the Environment and Rural Affairs had not done enough in recent years to improve supply chain resilience.

articles.summary: A magnitude 5.2 earthquake struck Myanmar at 10.36 pm (local time) on Friday. No injuries have been reported so far.
articles.body: A magnitude 5.2 earthquake struck Myanmar at 10.36 pm (local time) on Friday. No injuries have been reported so far.Myanmar is highly vulnerable to earthquakes and tsunamis due to its location at the convergence of four major tectonic plates: the Indian, Eurasian, Sunda and Burma plates. The continuous interaction between these plates, along with geological activity along the country's extensive coastline, contributes to its seismic risk.The Sagaing Fault, a 1,400-kilometre transform fault that cuts through Myanmar, is a major source of this risk. Linking the Andaman spreading centre with a northern collision zone, the fault increases earthquake risks for Sagaing, Mandalay, Bago and Yangon, which together account for 46 per cent of the country's population.Although Yangon lies at a considerable distance from the fault, its high population density makes it vulnerable to earthquakes. articles.summary: Retired govt employee, 71, dies after scooter skids and truck runs over him in South Extension, Delhi; truck driver arrested, case filed under BNS.
articles.body: New Delhi: A 71-year-old retired govt employee died after his scooter allegedly skidded on Ring Road in south Delhi’s South Extension and he was run over by a truck Thursday, police said. The truck driver has been arrested and the vehicle seized.The accident took place around noon in front of a restaurant in South Extension Part-II. The deceased, identified as Lal Dev Shah, was riding his scooter when he allegedly lost control of the vehicle and fell onto the road. A truck passing by ran over him, leaving him critically injured, according to police.Police were informed about the accident and a team reached the spot. Shah was taken for medical assistance, but he could not be saved. His body was subsequently sent for the required legal formalities.A case has been registered at Kotla Mubarakpur police station under Sections 281 and 106(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). Section 281 deals with rash driving or riding on a public way, while Section 106(1) pertains to causing death by negligence.The stretch where the accident took place is a busy road, with a steady flow of vehicles throughout the day. The Ring Road corridor witnesses considerable traffic, particularly during peak hours, as commuters use it to travel between different parts of the city.The truck driver, identified as Brijlal Yadav (46), was arrested in connection with the case. Police have seized the truck allegedly involved in the accident for further analysis.Investigators are looking into the sequence of events leading to the accident, including how the scooter skidded and the circumstances in which the truck ran over the rider. Police are also expected to examine available evidence from the accident site to establish the exact cause of the crash.Similar fatal road accidents involving heavy vehicles have been reported in the city in recent months.In Sept, four people installing CCTV cameras for Delhi Traffic Police were killed and two others injured when a dumper truck collided with a stationary crane and a parked autorickshaw in Sarita Vihar.In Aug, a 53-year-old woman died after being hit by a dumper truck in southeast Delhi’s Nehru Place. articles.body: New Delhi: A suspected gang war was averted after Delhi Police arrested an alleged shooter linked to the Naveen Bali-Neeraj Bawana gang, who was reportedly on his way to target a member of the rival Gogi gang in Alipur, police said.Eight firearms, including three semi-automatic pistols and five country-made pistols, along with 30 live cartridges, were recovered from the accused.The accused, Harsh (22), a resident of Nangal Thakran village in Bawana, was apprehended near Ring Road under Yudhister Setu in Kashmere Gate around 11.55 pm Thursday.Joint CP (Central) Madhur Verma said police had received specific intelligence that a suspected shooter associated with the Naveen Bali-Neeraj Bawana gang was carrying weapons and intended to travel to Alipur to eliminate a rival gang member.Acting on the input, a police team laid a trap near the bridge and intercepted Harsh as he arrived on a blue scooter from the Civil Lines side.During a search, police allegedly recovered a semi-automatic pistol loaded with five live cartridges from his waistband. articles.summary: Indrakeeladri Durga temple in Vijayawada returns to normal after Dasara rush; Bhavani devotees thin out and all service counters reopen Friday afternoon.
articles.body: Vijayawada: Normal activities resumed at Sri Durga Malleswara Swamy Varla Devasthanam on Indrakeeladri on Friday afternoon as the rush of Bhavani devotees eased, with all service counters reopened for devotees.The rush, which continued until Friday morning, saw thousands of Bhavani devotees visit the temple, offer their irumudis and conclude their Bhavani Deeksha after darshan of the presiding deity. With the crowd thinning by afternoon, the temple premises returned to a relatively peaceful atmosphere.Temple executive officer VK Seena Naik directed officials to make all service counters, including those for darshan tickets, laddu prasadam, puja tickets and donations, fully operational from Friday afternoon to ensure that regular devotees do not face inconvenience.Temple staff deployed on special duties during the Dasara Sarannavaratri festivities, including at the ghat road, queue lines, holding areas and prasadam distribution points, returned to their regular departmental duties after the rush subsided.The EO also instructed staff to ensure the smooth conduct of daily annaprasadam distribution, arjitha sevas and Antaralaya darshan as per the prescribed procedures.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Vijayawada | Silver Rate in Vijayawada | Bank Holidays in Vijayawada | Public Holidays in Vijayawada | Petrol Price in Vijayawada | Diesel Price in Vijayawada | CNG Price in Vijayawada | LPG Price in VijayawadaStay updated with the latest Vijayawada news. articles.title: Delayed transfers cleared: Gujarat relieves primary teachers waiting since 2022
articles.summary: Gujarat orders 100% relieving of primary teachers awaiting district/taluka transfers since 2022-23, using gyan sahayaks to maintain 50% staffing.
articles.body: Ahmedabad: Gujarat education department has ordered the complete relieving of primary school teachers who have been awaiting district or taluka transfers since 2022-23 despite receiving transfer orders. The decision provides relief to teachers whose transfers were stalled due to the rule requiring schools to maintain at least 50% of their sanctioned staff strength.The decision follows representations by Primary Teachers’ Association and Prathmik Shaikshik Mahasangh. Teachers posted in remote districts such as Kutch, Devbhumi Dwarka, Dahod, Narmada and Chhota Udepur have been particularly affected, with many waiting for years to move closer to their hometowns.According to the department’s instructions, districts will calculate the staffing strength of gyan sahayaks to determine whether the required 50% staffing level can be maintained. If the requirement is fulfilled, teachers awaiting transfers will be relieved immediately.Where vacancies arise because teachers are transferred but cannot be relieved due to staff shortages, the posts will be treated as vacant and filled by appointing gyan sahayaks from the waiting list. This arrangement is intended to facilitate transfers without disrupting school functioning.The department has also directed that every school must have at least one teacher present throughout the process. articles.title: Dhillon slams Mann over SIR speech in assembly
articles.summary: Punjab BJP chief Kewal Singh Dhillon criticises CM Bhagwant Mann’s Assembly speech on electoral roll SIR, saying the state ran it and must own any errors.
articles.body: Chandigarh: Punjab BJP president Kewal Singh Dhillon on Friday slammed chief minister Bhagwant Mann over his speech in the Punjab assembly regarding the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.Referring to the SIR exercise in Punjab in which final electoral rolls were published on Oct 12, Dhillon, in a written statement, said, “You (CM Mann) run the state govt, your officers carried out the exercise, and you yourself conducted the SIR. Now you are the one raising questions about it.”Dhillon pointed out, “From deputy commissioners and sub-divisional magistrates (SDMs) to officials at the booth level, all the personnel involved were under the state govt’s administration. The Centre had no role in the exercise.”He asked, “If your officers made mistakes during the SIR, why did your party leaders visit the Election Commission and claim that everything was in order?”Dhillon stated, “While the CM was alleging irregularities in the SIR in the assembly, leaders from his own party were telling the Election Commission that everything was fine.” He challenged Mann to “identify even a single voter in the state whose name had been wrongly deleted from the electoral rolls”.The Punjab BJP further stated, “If any irregularities had indeed occurred, it would be a serious matter for which the state govt itself would be responsible.”He described Mann’s remarks as “evidence” of what he called “an incompetent govt”, alleging that “it had lost its ability to think clearly and make sound decisions”.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. articles.title: Left parties field 20 candidates for GVMC elections
articles.summary: Left parties field 20 candidates in GVMC Visakhapatnam polls; CPM 14, CPI 6, with AAP support, urging voters to defeat TDP-JSP-BJP alliance.
articles.body: Visakhapatnam: Left parties, including the CPM and CPI, have fielded 20 candidates in the GVMC elections in Visakhapatnam. While 14 candidates are contesting from the CPM in different wards of the city, six belong to the CPI. Four AAP candidates are also in the fray. The Left parties have also announced support for independent candidate B Ramani from Ward 119.Addressing a press meet on Friday, CPM leader Ch Narsinga Rao and CPI state assistant secretary JV Satyanarayana Murthy, along with other Left and AAP leaders, called upon voters to defeat the TDP-Jana Sena-BJP alliance.“The coalition is handing over public resources to corporates and increasing the burden on ordinary people. We appeal to people to elect our corporator candidates to ensure city development, pollution control and corruption-free governance,” the Left leaders said.The leaders said the CPM, CPI, MCPI, CPI (ML), Prajaporu, SUCI(C) and AAP had decided to contest the elections together to provide an alternative and accountable administration in the GVMC.“The state govt has failed to control rising air pollution and ensure an adequate drinking water supply in the city. Allocating green hills for data centres would only worsen pollution and water shortages. The government is granting permissions for data centre projects despite growing opposition to them worldwide. It has also failed to take adequate measures to control the rising prices of essential commodities. articles.title: B’deshi with links to illegal cross-border activity held in Dhubri
articles.summary: Assam police in Dhubri arrested suspected Bangladeshi national Robial Sheikh for questioning over alleged links to cross-border illegal activity.
articles.body: Dhubri: Lakshiganj police in Dhubri district arrested Robial Sheikh, a suspected Bangladeshi national, in Udmari and shifted him to Dhubri for questioning by the Crime Branch.According to police sources, Sheikh was detained during an operation in Udmari and questioned at Bilasipara police station to establish his identity and nationality. He was later taken to Dhubri for further interrogation.Bilasipara OC Biswajit Bhadra told TOI that Sheikh said he was from Lalmonirhat in Bangladesh, near Dhubri district.The source said Sheikh was suspected of being linked to a larger network involved in cross-border illegal activities.In June, another Bangladeshi national, identified as 32-year-old Muqtar Hussain from Dinajpur, was apprehended by the BSF’s 89th Battalion and later arrested by Assam police in Dhubri district. articles.title: Overnight rain leaves Madurai flooded
articles.summary: Overnight rain flooded Madurai; pumps cleared most areas in 6–7 hours, but Sellur stayed inundated due to blocked drains. More rain forecast, alerts issued.
articles.body: Madurai: Madurai returned to normal within six to seven hours of flooding triggered by overnight rain, as a prepared corporation machinery and TVK MLAs on the ground helped clear water from most neighbourhoods by Friday morning. Sellur, however, remained inundated until evening, with residents blaming poorly timed Pandhalkudi channel works for worsening the flooding.Corporation commissioner Gaurav Kumar, who inspected low-lying areas along the Vaigai in the early hours, said around 80 pumps, including 35 heavy-duty units, and two rented super-sucker machines were kept ready for deployment across 180 identified flood-prone spots. The arrangements helped clear water within hours from Goripalayam, Anna Nagar, Mattuthavani and several other areas.In Sellur, however, residents were furious as knee-deep rainwater mixed with sewage entered hundreds of houses along the 50-foot and 60-foot roads and remained stagnant until evening. Drainage outlets blocked during the ongoing Pandhalkudi channel construction prevented water from flowing out. “Many have no choice, otherwise we would have evacuated and left the area a long time ago,” said resident Subbulakshmi, describing recurring damage to houses.Gaurav attributed the flooding to Sellur’s low-lying terrain and said the water resources department had deployed an excavator to remove silt and restore drainage. Madurai North MLA A Kallanai, who inspected the area, said workers were addressing the problem and expected to complete restoration within half an hour.Access posed another challenge in Muthuramalingapuram and Swarajyapuram, where van-mounted pumps could not enter narrow streets. The corporation now plans to deploy pumps mounted on hired three-wheelers before the next spell of rain.Meanwhile, the 400-metre stretch between Madurai Junction and Periyar bus stand once again flooded, affecting passengers. A ₹10.53-crore drainage overhaul has already been tendered to address the recurring problem.With more rain forecast for Madurai over the weekend, authorities have warned residents against venturing near the Vaigai and other riverbanks because of the risk of sudden flooding.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Madurai | Silver Rate in Madurai | Bank Holidays in Madurai | Public Holidays in Madurai | Madurai AQI | Weather in Madurai | Petrol Price in Madurai | Diesel Price in Madurai | CNG Price in Madurai | LPG Price in MaduraiStay updated with the latest Madurai news. articles.title: Vizag motorists seek crackdown on stray cattle
articles.summary: Vizag motorists urge GVMC to crack down on stray cattle blocking roads, citing frequent accidents and poor enforcement; call for impounding, fines and cattle shed.
articles.body: Visakhapatnam: As parties and candidates prepare to contest the Greater Visakhapatnam Municipal Corporation (GVMC) elections, motorists in parts of the city have raised concerns over stray animals obstructing traffic and causing accidents. They demanded that the civic body implement a comprehensive solution to tackle the menace.Motorists say cattle owners in parts of the city let their livestock onto roads, where they feed on garbage bins and litter. Accidents often happen as the stray animals feed on vegetation on the medians. Residents have seen stray cattle crossing roads near China Waltair, Appughar, MVP Colony, Marikavalasa, Kommadi, Bheemili, Arilova, and a few other places in Vizag city, with residents saying the animals also enter highways and the beach road stretch in the city.Stray cattle continue to pose a road safety risk in parts of Vizag, with neither GVMC authorities nor former corporators taking measures despite repeated complaints, MVP Colony resident D Sudhakar said.The situation was particularly alarming during evenings and early mornings, when low visibility increased the risk of crashes, he said. Stray dogs and pigs also obstructed traffic and caused accidents, he added.Stray cattle abandoned on roads pose safety and sanitation risks, besides damaging parked vehicles, parks, roadside plantations and standing crops in adjoining areas.Residents said the lack of strict enforcement and penalties, including impounding cattle, encouraged owners to abandon unproductive animals.Madhurawada resident A Satyanarayana said the civic body had announced plans to seize stray cattle and fine owners for allowing livestock onto roads, but these measures were not fully implemented.
